contentObjective: I can estimate the percent of a number using benchmark percents, rounding, and compatible numbers.
languageObjective: I can explain an estimate using the words about, benchmark, and compatible numbers.

vocabulary.definition: A reasoned answer that is close enough to be useful, found without exact computation.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una respuesta razonada, lo bastante cercana para ser útil, sin cálculo exacto.
vocabulary.example: 8.6% of 216 is about 10% of 220, which is 22.
vocabulary.cloze: A reasoned answer close enough to be useful is an ___.

examples.text: “About 20 pounds” when the exact answer is 18.576
examples.why: Close enough to plan with, found without exact computation.
That is the exact answer, not an estimate.

vocabulary.definition: A friendly percent — 1%, 10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% — used as a landmark for estimating.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un porcentaje amigable — 1%, 10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% — que sirve de punto de referencia.
vocabulary.example: 4 GB of 6 GB sits between the 50% and 75% marks.
vocabulary.visual: 1% · 10% · 25% · 50% · 75% · 100% — the landmarks you can find mentally.
vocabulary.cloze: A friendly percent used as a landmark, like 10% or 25%, is a ___ ___.

examples.text: Using 50% because half of an amount is easy
examples.why: It is one of the percents you can find in your head.

examples.text: Using 37% because it is in the problem
examples.why: It is exact, but nothing about it is mentally friendly.

vocabulary.definition: Numbers close to the originals that are easy to compute with mentally.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Números cercanos a los originales con los que es fácil calcular mentalmente.
vocabulary.visual: 8.6% of 216 → 10% of 220: both nudged to numbers that divide nicely.
vocabulary.cloze: Numbers close to the originals that are easy to compute with are ___ ___.

examples.why: 200 is close by and 10% of it is instant.
It is easy to compute, but far too far from the original.

vocabulary.definition: Two parallel number lines that pair amounts with their percents at the same positions.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos rectas paralelas que emparejan cantidades con sus porcentajes en las mismas posiciones.
vocabulary.example: GB on top, percent on the bottom: 1.5 GB lines up with 25%.
vocabulary.cloze: Two parallel lines pairing amounts with their percents form a ___ ___ ___.

examples.text: Dollars marked on one line and percents on the other, lined up
examples.why: Matching positions pair an amount with its percent.

examples.text: One number line with only percents on it
examples.why: With nothing to pair against, there is no second quantity.

vocabulary.definition: The quantity that counts as 100% in a problem — and it can change between questions.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La cantidad que representa el 100% en un problema, y puede cambiar entre preguntas.
vocabulary.example: First the whole is 6 GB; for the photos question the whole becomes the 4 GB used.
vocabulary.visual: “Of the USED storage” makes 4 GB the whole — not the 6 GB total.
vocabulary.cloze: The quantity that counts as 100% in a problem is ___ ___.

examples.text: The 60 students in the class when 18 of them walk
examples.why: It is the amount the percent is measured against.
That is the part; the percent describes it, it is not the whole.

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: The Food Drive
revealWordProblem.text:
The organizers of a food drive set a new goal for a second food drive. They hope to collect 140% as many cans as they did last time, when they collected 145 cans.
Question: About how many cans can the organizers expect to collect? Explain your reasoning.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Estimate with benchmark percents. 145 rounds to 150, and 140% is 100% + 40%. 100% of 150 is 150, and 40% of 150 is 60, so 150 + 60 = 210 cans — about 200. Checking exactly: 1.4 × 145 = 203, which is close to the estimate, so about 200 cans is a reasonable expectation.

questions.stem: Margaret's phone has 6 GB of storage and 4 GB is used. About what percent is used?
questions.explanation: 4 out of 6 is 2/3, which is about 67%, so 'about 70%' is the reasonable estimate.
choiceFeedback: 25% of 6 GB would be only 1.5 GB.
That reads the 4 GB as 40% — but the whole is 6, not 10.
More than 100% would mean using more storage than the phone has.
hints: 4 out of 6 is the same as 2 out of 3.
Two-thirds is close to which benchmark?
questions.stemEs: El teléfono de Margaret tiene 6 GB de almacenamiento y 4 GB están usados. ¿Aproximadamente qué porcentaje está usado?
questions.explanationEs: 4 de 6 es 2/3, que es aproximadamente 67%, así que 'aproximadamente 70%' es la estimación razonable.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál es el entero?
4 de 6 es lo mismo que 2 de 3.
¿Dos tercios está cerca de cuál punto de referencia?

questions.stem: On the double number line for 6 GB, what amount lines up with 25%?
questions.explanation: 25% of 6 GB is one quarter of 6, which is 1.5 GB.
choiceFeedback: That divides 6 by 4.8 rather than by 4.
2.5 GB would be more than a third of the storage.
4 GB lines up near 67%, not 25%.
questions.stemEs: En la recta numérica doble para 6 GB, ¿qué cantidad se alinea con 25%?
questions.explanationEs: 25% de 6 GB es una cuarta parte de 6, que es 1.5 GB.
hintsEs: 25% significa una cuarta parte.
Una cuarta parte de 6.

questions.stem: Which benchmark percents make good landmarks on a number line?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 25 (and 10) are friendly landmarks because their amounts are easy to compute.
choiceFeedback: Those percents are no easier to compute with than the original problem.
50% alone leaves most of the line unmarked.
100% alone gives you nothing to compare against in the middle.
hints: Which percents can you find mentally?
Quarters and tenths are the friendly ones.
questions.stemEs: ¿Cuáles porcentajes de referencia sirven bien como puntos guía en una recta numérica?
questions.explanationEs: Los múltiplos de 25 (y de 10) son puntos de referencia amigables porque sus cantidades son fáciles de calcular.
hintsEs: ¿Cuáles porcentajes puedes hallar mentalmente?
Los cuartos y los décimos son los amigables.

steps: 1. Use benchmark percents: 10% (move decimal left 1), 1% (move left 2), 50% (half), 25% (quarter)
3. Round numbers to compatible values for quick mental estimates
reviewHighlights.watchOut: Keeping the same whole for every question — when the problem says 'of the used storage,' the whole changes from 6 GB to 4 GB, and estimates anchored to the old whole are wrong before any arithmetic happens.

level1.stem: To estimate 8.6% of 216 by rounding, which numbers should you use?
level1.explanation: 8.6% rounds to 10% and 216 rounds to 220 — both are close to the originals and easy to compute.
choiceFeedback: 1% is far below 8.6%, so the estimate would be far too small.
300 is far from 216, so the estimate drifts too far.
86% misplaces the decimal — that is ten times too large.
hints: Round each number to something friendly.
216 is close to which round number?
level1.stemEs: Para estimar el 8.6% de 216 por redondeo, ¿qué números debes usar?
level1.explanationEs: 8.6% se redondea a 10% y 216 se redondea a 220 — ambos están cerca de los originales y son fáciles de calcular.
hintsEs: Redondea cada número a algo amigable.
¿8.6% está cerca de cuál punto de referencia?
¿216 está cerca de cuál número redondo?

choiceFeedback: That moves the decimal two places instead of one.
That is 20% of 220.
That is 100% of 220, not 10%.
hintsEs: Escribe 10% como decimal.

level1.stem: The word 'approximately' appears in the storage problem. What does it tell you about the answer you need?
level1.modelAnswer: It tells me an exact answer is not required — I can use benchmarks and rounding to get close, and 'about 70%' counts as correct.
sentenceStems: So instead of computing exactly, I can ___ .
level1.stemEs: La palabra 'aproximadamente' aparece en el problema del almacenamiento. ¿Qué te dice sobre la respuesta que necesitas?

level1.stem: (Lesson 4.1) What does the word percent mean?
level1.explanation: Percent means per hundred, which is why every percent can be written as a fraction with a denominator of 100.
choiceFeedback: Per ten would be a tenth, not a percent.
Per thousand is a different comparison entirely.
"Part" does not say how big the whole is; a percent always compares to 100.
hints: Look at the second half of the word: cent.
A century is 100 years; a cent is 1/100 of a dollar.
level1.explanationEs: Por ciento significa por cada cien, y por eso todo porcentaje se puede escribir como una fracción con denominador 100.
hintsEs: Mira la segunda parte de la palabra: ciento.
Un siglo son 100 años; un centavo es 1/100 de dólar.
Por ciento = por cada 100.

level1.stem: (Lesson 4.1) 3 out of every 10 students walk to school. What percent is that?
level1.explanation: Multiply both terms of the ratio by 10 to compare to 100: 3 out of 10 becomes 30 out of 100, or 30%.
choiceFeedback: 3 out of 100 would be 3%, but the ratio here is out of 10.
10 is the second term of the original ratio, not the percent.
That adds the two numbers instead of scaling the ratio.
hints: A percent compares to 100, so rewrite the ratio out of 100.
What do you multiply 10 by to get 100?
Multiply BOTH terms by that same number.
level1.stemEs: 3 de cada 10 estudiantes caminan a la escuela. ¿Qué porcentaje es eso?
level1.explanationEs: Multiplica los dos términos de la razón por 10 para compararla con 100: 3 de 10 se convierte en 30 de 100, o sea 30%.
hintsEs: Un porcentaje compara con 100, así que reescribe la razón sobre 100.
¿Por cuánto multiplicas 10 para obtener 100?
Multiplica AMBOS términos por ese mismo número.

level2.stem: The Green-Team recycled 216 pounds; 8.6% was metal. Using compatible numbers 10% and 200, the estimate is:
choiceFeedback: That is 1% of 200 — the decimal moved one place too far.
That reads 8.6% as 86 pounds.
That subtracts 8 from 216 instead of taking a percent.
level2.stemEs: El Equipo Verde recicló 216 libras; 8.6% era metal. Usando los números compatibles 10% y 200, la estimación es:
hintsEs: Escribe 10% como decimal.
Un décimo de 200.

level2.stem: Photos use 3.5 GB of the 4 GB of used storage. About what percent of the USED storage is photos?
level2.explanation: The whole is 4 GB here. 75% of 4 is 3 GB and 100% is 4 GB; 3.5 sits midway — about 87%.
choiceFeedback: That reads 3.5 GB as 35% — the whole is 4, not 10.
That uses 6 GB as the whole, but the question asks about the USED storage.
3.5 out of 4 is clearly below 100%, but not that close to it.
hints: What is the whole for THIS question?
3.5 of 4 is between the 75% and 100% marks.
level2.stemEs: Las fotos usan 3.5 GB de los 4 GB de almacenamiento usado. ¿Aproximadamente qué porcentaje del almacenamiento USADO son las fotos?
level2.explanationEs: Aquí el entero es 4 GB. 75% de 4 son 3 GB y 100% son 4 GB; 3.5 queda a la mitad — aproximadamente 87%.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál es el entero para ESTA pregunta?
El entero es 4 GB, no 6.
3.5 de 4 está entre las marcas de 75% y 100%.

level2.stem: Why did the whole change between the two storage questions?
choices: The phone gained storage between the questions
The whole never changes in a percent problem
The second question asks about the used storage, so 4 GB becomes 100%
Because photos are more important than mail
level2.explanation: Each percent question defines its own whole. 'Of the used storage' makes the 4 GB the new 100%.
choiceFeedback: The phone's capacity never changed — the QUESTION changed.
The whole is set by the question, and this pair of questions sets it differently.
Importance has nothing to do with which quantity is the whole.
hints: Which quantity is that question about?
level2.stemEs: ¿Por qué cambió el entero entre las dos preguntas del almacenamiento?
level2.explanationEs: Cada pregunta de porcentaje define su propio entero. 'Del almacenamiento usado' convierte los 4 GB en el nuevo 100%.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer: 'Del almacenamiento USADO…'
¿De cuál cantidad trata esa pregunta?
Esa cantidad se convierte en el 100%.

level2.explanation: 24% is about 25%, and 81 is about 80. One quarter of 80 is 20.
choiceFeedback: 2 is about 2.5% of 81 — far below 24%.
8 is about 10% of 81, not 24%.
40 would be about half of 81, but 24% is about a quarter.
level2.stemEs: Estima el 24% de 81 con puntos de referencia.
level2.explanationEs: 24% es aproximadamente 25%, y 81 es aproximadamente 80. Una cuarta parte de 80 es 20.
hintsEs: ¿A cuál punto de referencia se acerca el 24%?
25% es una cuarta parte.
Una cuarta parte de 80.

level2.stem: Your estimate for 8.6% of 216 was 22 pounds (using 10% of 220). Is the exact answer higher or lower than 22?
choices: Higher, because rounding always shrinks the answer
Lower, because both 10% and 220 rounded UP
level2.explanation: 8.6% went up to 10% and 216 went up to 220, so the estimate overshoots — the exact answer (about 18.6) is lower.
choiceFeedback: Rounding can push an estimate either way; here both pushes were upward.
Exactness is what we gave up when we rounded.
You CAN tell, by looking at which direction each rounding moved.
hints: Which way did each number round?
So the estimate is a little high.
level2.stemEs: Tu estimación del 8.6% de 216 fue 22 libras (usando 10% de 220). ¿La respuesta exacta es mayor o menor que 22?
level2.explanationEs: 8.6% subió a 10% y 216 subió a 220, así que la estimación se pasa — la respuesta exacta (aproximadamente 18.6) es menor.
hintsEs: ¿Hacia dónde se redondeó cada número?
Los dos se redondearon hacia arriba.
Así que la estimación queda un poco alta.

level3.stem: A jacket originally priced at $78.99 is on sale for 25% off. Which is the best estimate of the discount amount?
choiceFeedback: That is about one eighth of $80. 25% is one QUARTER, so divide $80 by 4.
That is half of $80. 25% is half of 50%, so halve it once more.
That is about 10% of $80. 25% is two and a half times that much.
level3.explanation: Round $78.99 to $80. 25% is 1/4 of the whole. 1/4 of $80 is $20.

level3.stem: Two students estimate 8.6% of 216. Ana uses 10% of 220 = 22. Ben uses 10% of 200 = 20. Whose estimate is closer to the exact answer, 18.576?
choices: Ben's — 20 is 1.4 away; Ana's 22 is 3.4 away
level3.explanation: Exact is 18.576. Ben's 20 misses by about 1.4; Ana's 22 misses by about 3.4. Compatible numbers won this one.
choiceFeedback: 22 − 18.576 = 3.424, which is farther than Ben's 1.424.
The two distances are 1.4 and 3.4 — not equal.
Both are valid estimates; the question is which lands closer.
level3.stemEs: Dos estudiantes estiman el 8.6% de 216. Ana usa 10% de 220 = 22. Ben usa 10% de 200 = 20. ¿Cuál estimación está más cerca de la respuesta exacta, 18.576?
level3.explanationEs: Lo exacto es 18.576. El 20 de Ben falla por unos 1.4; el 22 de Ana falla por unos 3.4. Los números compatibles ganaron esta vez.
hintsEs: Halla la distancia de cada uno a 18.576.
1.4 contra 3.4.

level3.stem: For which problem is ESTIMATING clearly the right tool, rather than exact computation?
choices: Deciding if a $58 jacket at 25% off fits your $45 budget
Programming a bank to compute interest on every account
level3.explanation: A quick benchmark — 25% of 60 is 15, so about $43 — answers the budget question; the others need exactness.
choiceFeedback: Bank interest must be computed exactly, to the cent.
Medicine doses can never be 'about right'.
Test scoring has to be exact for every student.
hints: Money decisions you make in an aisle are estimates.
The other three carry real risk if inexact.
level3.stemEs: ¿Para cuál problema es ESTIMAR claramente la herramienta correcta, en vez del cálculo exacto?
level3.explanationEs: Un punto de referencia rápido — 25% de 60 es 15, o sea unos $43 — responde la pregunta del presupuesto; los demás casos necesitan exactitud.
hintsEs: ¿Dónde basta con 'lo bastante cerca'?
Las decisiones de dinero que tomas en un pasillo de la tienda son estimaciones.
Las otras tres tienen un riesgo real si no son exactas.

level3.stem: Write your own estimation problem about percent, using a real situation from your life. Then solve it with a benchmark and say whether your estimate runs high or low.
level3.modelAnswer: My playlist has 62 songs and about 48% are hip-hop. 48% is about 50%, and 62 is about 60, so about 30 songs. Both roundings moved in opposite directions, so my estimate is very close.
sentenceStems: ___% is near the benchmark ___ , so my estimate is ___ .
level3.stemEs: Escribe tu propio problema de estimación sobre porcentajes, usando una situación real de tu vida. Luego resuélvelo con un punto de referencia y di si tu estimación queda alta o baja.

level3.stem: A store marks a $79.95 item 32% off. Which mental estimate best checks the discount?
choices: About one third of 80, so about $26 off
level3.explanation: 32% is near the benchmark 1/3, and $79.95 is nearly 80. A third of 80 is about 26.7.
choiceFeedback: That is 4% of 80, a misplaced decimal.
Percent is not a dollar count — 32% of 80 is not automatically $32 (though here it lands nearby, the reasoning is wrong).
Half would be 50%, far above 32%.
level3.stemEs: Una tienda rebaja 32% un artículo de $79.95. ¿Cuál estimación mental revisa mejor el descuento?
level3.explanationEs: 32% está cerca del punto de referencia 1/3, y $79.95 es casi 80. Un tercio de 80 es aproximadamente 26.7.
hintsEs: ¿A cuál fracción de referencia se acerca el 32%?
Un tercio.
Un tercio de 80.
